notes.summary: Blood Relations questions describe family links through plain statements, introductions ('pointing to a photo...') or symbol codes (A + B means A is the mother of B), and ask how two people are related. SSC CGL usually has 1-2 such questions, often built around a gender trap or an in-law link.
keyPoints: Draw a family tree: + for male, − for female, a horizontal line for a married couple, a vertical line for parent and child, and the same level for the same generation.
Decode introductions starting from the end. 'My mother's husband's only daughter': mother's husband = father, so his only daughter = my sister (if I am male) or me (if I am female).
Father's or mother's brother = uncle; father's or mother's sister = aunt; their children = cousins; a brother's or sister's children = nephew or niece.
In-laws: a spouse's brother or a sister's husband = brother-in-law; a son's wife = daughter-in-law; a daughter's husband = son-in-law.
Never assume gender from words like child, parent, sibling or spouse. Only son, daughter, brother, sister, father, mother, husband, wife (or a clearly gendered name) fix it.
Coded relations: translate each symbol into words from left to right and write the chain on paper (P + Q − R × S → P is mother of Q, Q is brother of R, R is father of S).
For 'which expression shows that X is the uncle of Y', X must be the brother of someone who is Y's parent.
Count generations: grandparents are 2 levels up and great-grandparents 3. People on the same level are siblings, cousins, spouses or in-laws.
traps: Assuming gender: 'B is the daughter of C' does not tell you whether C is the father or the mother.
Mixing up the direction: 'How is A related to B' asks for A's role, not B's (nephew vs uncle).
Reading a code backwards, e.g. taking A × B to mean B is the father of A.
Missing that a speaker can be the person they describe ('the only daughter of my father' can be the speaker herself).
notes.examTip: Always sketch the tree with gender marks. Even a 10-second sketch prevents most mistakes in introduction and coded questions.

questions.text: Ravi's mother's husband has only one daughter, Neha. How is Neha related to Ravi?
questions.explanation:
Ravi's mother's husband is Ravi's father.
The only daughter of Ravi's father is Ravi's sister.
So Neha is Ravi's sister.

questions.text: P is the brother of Q. Q is the son of R. Which of the following is definitely true?
options: R is a parent of P
questions.explanation:
Q is the son of R, and P is Q's brother, so P is also R's child.
We are never told whether R is male or female, so we cannot say 'father' or 'mother', and nothing is said about age.
The only certain fact is that R is a parent of P.

questions.text: Pointing to a boy, Kiran said, 'He is the son of my father's sister.' How is the boy related to Kiran?
questions.explanation:
Kiran's father's sister is Kiran's aunt.
The son of one's aunt is one's cousin.
So the boy is Kiran's cousin.

questions.text: A + B means A is the mother of B; A − B means A is the brother of B; A × B means A is the father of B; A ÷ B means A is the sister of B. If P + Q − R × S, how is P related to S?
questions.explanation:
P + Q: P is the mother of Q.
Q − R: Q is the brother of R, so R is also P's child.
R × S: R is the father of S.
P is the mother of S's father, so P is S's grandmother.

questions.text: A + B means A is the mother of B; A − B means A is the brother of B; A × B means A is the father of B; A ÷ B means A is the sister of B. Which of the following expressions means that M is the uncle of N?
questions.explanation:
An uncle is the brother of a parent.
M − X × N: M is the brother of X, and X is the father of N, so M is N's paternal uncle.
M ÷ X × N makes M the aunt, M × X − N makes M the father of N, and M + X − N makes M the mother of N.
So the answer is M − X × N.

questions.text: Pointing to a lady, Arun said, 'She is the daughter of the woman who is the mother of my mother's husband.' How is the lady related to Arun?
questions.explanation:
Arun's mother's husband is Arun's father.
The mother of Arun's father is Arun's grandmother.
The grandmother's daughter is Arun's father's sister.
So the lady is Arun's aunt (his father's sister).

questions.text: A is the son of B. B is the sister of C. C is the father of D. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation:
B is A's mother, and B is the sister of C, so C is A's maternal uncle.
D is C's child.
The children of a sister and a brother are cousins, so A is D's cousin.

questions.text: In a family of six members P, Q, R, S, T and U, P is the father of R and S, and Q is P's wife. R is a married man and S is his unmarried sister. T is P's daughter-in-law, and U is Q's grandson. How is S related to U?
questions.explanation:
P and Q are a couple with two children: a son R and a daughter S.
T is P's daughter-in-law, so T is the wife of P's only son, R.
U is Q's grandson. S is unmarried, so U is the son of R and T.
S is the sister of U's father, so S is U's aunt.

questions.text: A and B are a married couple. C and D are brothers. C is the brother of A. How is D related to B?
questions.explanation:
C is A's brother and D is C's brother, so D is also A's brother.
B is A's spouse, and a spouse's brother is a brother-in-law.
So D is B's brother-in-law, whether A is the husband or the wife.

questions.text: P @ Q means P is the father of Q; P # Q means P is the wife of Q; P $ Q means P is the daughter of Q; P & Q means P is the brother of Q. If A @ B # C @ D & F, how is D related to A?
questions.explanation:
A @ B: A is the father of B.
B # C: B is the wife of C, so B is A's daughter and C is A's son-in-law.
C @ D: C is the father of D, so D is the child of B and C.
D & F: D is the brother of F, so D is male.
D is the son of A's daughter, so D is A's grandson.

questions.text: A family has six members A, B, C, D, E and F. A and B are a married couple, A being the male member. C is the brother of A. D is the only son of C, and E is D's sister. B is the daughter-in-law of F, whose husband has died. How is E related to F?
questions.explanation:
B is F's daughter-in-law and B is A's wife, so F is A's parent. F had a husband, so F is A's mother.
C is A's brother, so C is also F's son.
D is C's son and E is D's sister, so E is C's daughter.
E is the daughter of F's son, so E is F's granddaughter.
